correctness.rationale: The finite-difference identity proves D(k) divides k+1; the published p-primary criterion isolates a unique large prime-power component. Prime exponent one gives exactly D=p. Higher exponents contribute a power-saving bound using a count of prime powers; the weighted prime number theorem and summable m powers give the two explicit coefficients for every fixed s>0. Exact-comparison code checks 39 initial GCDs and every row up to one million, but finite tests are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full text of Guo et al. arXiv:2606.22997 (2026) was inspected: it proves a zero-versus-positive GCD criterion, not an asymptotic of positive moments. The present fixed-real-s family and the exact second logarithmic term require a weighted prime-summation decomposition and exceptional prime-power control. Hong (2016) studies a distinct fixed-upper-index binomial GCD. Searches found no exact prior mean law. An unindexed prior derivation remains possible.

value.rationale: The recently solved GCD criterion is a pointwise problem; the natural global question is the size distribution of those GCDs. The result supplies every positive real power-moment asymptotic together with a universal zeta-derivative second term. A highly nonuniform rare-large-prime regime dominates all positive moments despite most indices contributing at the unit scale. This is a distinct analytical characterization, not a table recomputation, though it relies on classical PNT tools.
